title: Pedal Harp

altText: A tall harp with a curved neck at the top, a straight column at the front, and a wooden soundbox below, with many strings stretched between them.

context: A pedal harp has pedals at its base that change the pitch of the strings, which lets a player use many different notes on one instrument. The Met dates this French harp to about 1800 and lists wood and various materials. The record does not name the maker, so the details of its mechanism and decoration should be read from the image.

descriptions.k: This is a tall harp from France. It has many strings. A curved top, a straight pole, and a big wooden bottom hold the strings. It has pedals at the base. A player plucks the strings with their fingers. Can you count some strings?
descriptions.g12: This tall harp was made in France about 220 years ago. Many strings stretch between the curved top and the wooden bottom. Pedals near the floor change the notes. The player plucks the strings with their fingers. Which part do you think is the most important?
descriptions.g35: This pedal harp was made in France around 1800. Its strings stretch from a curved neck at the top to a wooden soundbox below, and a tall column helps hold the frame. Pedals at the base change the pitch of the strings so the harp can play more notes. The Met does not name the maker. Look at the frame and the strings. How do the shapes work together?
descriptions.g68: This French pedal harp, dated about 1800, shows the large harps that became popular in Europe around that time. Strings run between a curved neck and a wooden soundbox, and a column supports the frame. Pedals at the base change the pitch of the strings, so one harp can play in many keys. The Met records wood and various materials but no named maker. What can we learn from the form and decoration of an unsigned instrument?
descriptions.g910: This pedal harp from France, about 1800, belongs to a period when the harp became a fashionable and technically developing instrument. A curved neck, a column and a soundbox form a strong triangle that holds the strings under tension, and pedals at the base allow a player to alter the pitch of the strings. The record lists wood and various materials and names no maker. Consider how the harp's structure makes tension and balance visible, and how decoration may have connected it to the taste of its time.
descriptions.g1112: Dated to about 1800 and catalogued as French, this pedal harp comes from a period of intense experiment in harp design, when mechanisms for changing pitch were still evolving. The record names no maker and gives limited information on its mechanism or decoration, so claims about its type or maker's workshop should be hedged. The triangular frame, in which strings, neck, column and soundbox hold one another in tension, makes the instrument a study in engineering as well as a fashionable object, and invites reflection on how technical innovation and taste shaped musical culture.

teacherNote.context: A French pedal harp of about 1800 with no named maker in the record. The record does not describe its mechanism or decoration, so students should observe the image and compare it with other harps.
directions: Compare this harp with the Burmese saung-gauk or an arched harp: how is the frame different?
Stretch rubber bands of different lengths on a box to explore pitch and tension.
Discuss how an unsigned object can still serve as evidence.
